46: [6] The Foundlings' Hospital in Moscow, where 80 to 90 per cent. of the children die.
44: [4] Loud public wailing of this kind is customary, and considered indispensable, among the peasants.
42: [3] A formal request for forgiveness is customary among Russians, but it is often no mere formality. Nikíta's first reply is evasive; his second reply, “God will forgive you,” is the correct one sanctioned by custom.
40: [2] Peasant weddings are usually in autumn. They are forbidden in Lent, and soon after Easter the peasants become too busy to marry till harvest is over.

36: NIKÍTA [ bound ] No need to ask! I did it all myself. The design was mine, and the deed was mine. Take me where you like. I will say no more!
35: Nikíta is bound. AKOULÍNA [ goes and stands by his side ] I shall tell the truth! Ask me!
34: ELDER. There are witnesses enough here. POLICE OFFICER. We will have the examination at once.
31: AKÍM [ rapturously ] God will forgive you, my own son! [ Embraces him ] You have had no mercy on yourself, He will show mercy on you! God—God! It is He!
29: NIKÍTA. Wait, there's plenty of time! [ Bows to the ground before his father ] Father, dear father, forgive me too,—fiend that I am! You told me from the first, when I took to bad ways, you said then, “If a claw is caught, the bird is lost!” I would not listen to your words, dog that I was, and it has turned out as you said! Forgive me, for Christ's sake!
27: Men come up with their belts.
26: Silence. POLICE OFFICER. Bind him! The marriage is evidently off!
24: NIKÍTA. Don't shield me! I fear no one now! Forgive me, Christian Commune! [ Bows to the ground ].
23: AKOULÍNA. He raves! I told him to!
21: NIKÍTA. I smothered the baby in the cellar with a board! I sat on it and smothered it—and its bones crunched! [ Weeps ] And I buried it! I did it, all alone!
20: NIKÍTA. I poisoned the father, dog that I am, and I ruined the daughter! She was in my power, and I ruined her, and her baby! AKOULÍNA. True, that's true!
19: NIKÍTA. Wait, sir, let me finish! AKÍM [ with rapture ] Speak, my son! Tell everything—you'll feel better! Confess to God, don't fear men! God—God! It is He!
18: POLICE OFFICER. Repeat what you have said.
17: AKOULÍNA [ leaves the table ] Let me go! I shan't be married! He told me to, but I shan't now!
16: NIKÍTA. And, Akoulína, my sin is great towards you; I seduced you; forgive me in Christ's name! [ Bows to the ground before her ].
15: AKÍM. Let God's work be done, I mean, and then you, I mean, you do your business!
14: AKÍM. Eh, what a fellow you are; wait, I say! Don't talk, I mean, about, what d'ye call it, 'ditements! Here God's work is being done.… A man is confessing, I mean! And you, what d'ye call it … 'ditements! POLICE OFFICER. The Elder!
12: POLICE OFFICER. Mind, old man, and don't interfere! I have to draw up an indictment!
10: AKÍM [ to Police Officer ] Now you—with the bright buttons—I mean, you wait! Let him, what d'ye call it, speak out, I mean!
8: POLICE OFFICER. Seize him, and send for the Elder! We must draw up an indictment and have witnesses to it! Get up and come here!
7: AKÍM. Oh Lord, what sins, what sins!
6: AKOULÍNA [ jumps up ] He's telling lies! I know who did it! MATCHMAKER. What are you about? You sit still!
4: NIKÍTA. Akoulína, I poisoned him! Forgive me, in Christ's name!
2: AKÍM [ motions them back with his arms ] Wait! You lads, what d'ye call it, wait, I mean!
0: The folk come up and try to seize him.
